descriptionChirho: An absolute ruler or sovereign, used as a title of address to God or Christ, emphasizing supreme authority and ownership over all creation. This sense appears in prayers and doxologies where the speaker acknowledges God's total sovereignty. Multilingual evidence highlights the reverential register: Spanish 'Soberano' (Sovereign), Arabic 'سَيِّدُ' / 'السَّيِّد' (the Lord/Master), Hindi 'स्वामी' (lord/master in vocative), Korean '주인이시여' (O Master) / '주재이시며' (Sovereign ruler), Swahili 'Bwana Mkuu' (Great Lord). Attested in Luke 2:29 (Simeon's prayer), Acts 4:24 (the church's prayer), 2 Pet 2:1, Jude 1:4, Rev 6:10 (martyrs' cry).

A human master or owner, particularly of slaves or servants, denoting a person who holds legal authority over others in a household or economic relationship. Distinguished from the divine sense by its plural usage and explicitly human referent. Multilingual glosses reflect the domestic/economic register: Spanish 'amos' (masters/owners), Arabic 'سادَتَهُم' (their masters), Hindi 'स्वामियों' (masters, plural oblique), Korean '주인들을' (masters, accusative plural), Swahili 'mabwana' (masters/sirs). Attested in 1 Tim 6:1-2 (slaves and their masters), Titus 2:9 (slaves obeying masters), and 2 Tim 2:21 (useful to the master of the house).
